title: Charles Lyell's birth chart
metaDescription: Charles Lyell's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 22.7° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a conjunction: Mercury and Neptune within 0.1°, thinking wired to imagination. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 22.7° Scorpio: the third decan, whose classical sub-ruler is the Moon. A water sign, read here in its third face.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 10.8° Scorpio, Venus was at 4.5° Capricorn, Mars was at 19.3° Libra. Read together: a mind that absorbs before it argues; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that argues its way forward.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury to Neptune is the closest call of the day, a conjunction within 0.1°. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct. Behind it, Saturn trine Neptune at 0.8°, and Mercury trine Saturn at 0.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Venus opposes Saturn while both square Jupiter. A t-square aims the whole axis at its apex planet; the tradition reads it as the chart’s standing assignment. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. Mars in Libra at 19.3° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Cancer at 11.7° is in detriment. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 4 water, 2 earth, 2 air, 1 fire; by modality, 4 fixed, 4 cardinal, 1 mutable. Water reads the room before the room speaks — atmosphere first, analysis later. Jupiter and Saturn were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Virgo into Libra during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.0° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
